research_metadata.research_title: Dairy Farming Feasibility in Rural Kalaburagi: Aland, Afzalpur, Jevargi, Kalaburagi Taluks

business_profile.business_model: Production of cow/buffalo milk and sale to KMF/cooperatives, local market, and value-added customers
business_profile.description: Rearing of crossbred cows (HF, Jersey) and/or Murrah buffaloes for daily milk production, with sale to Kalaburagi-Bidar-Yadgir Milk Union (KMF network), private dairies, local hotels, and direct B2C. Suitable as supplementary activity for small/marginal farmers with 2-20 animals.

rural_suitability.reason: Kalaburagi PLP identifies dairy as key supplementary activity; 572 dairy cooperative societies exist in district, NABARD credit potential for dairy Rs 266.55 crore in 2022-23, and 70% population dependent on agriculture. Fodder can be grown on fallow lands.

KVK Kalaburagi, Department of Animal Husbandry

skills_required.skill: Daily operations - shed cleaning, heat detection, AI timing
skills_required.training_source: KMF Training Centre Kalaburagi, AH Dept

skills_required.skill: Milk quality testing and record keeping

taluk_comparison.recommendation_reason: Kalaburagi taluk offers highest demand due to urban population, best infrastructure (29 vet hospitals, 109 dispensaries, 572 DCS network, APMC, railway), assured KMF procurement with Rs 5/L incentive, and highest NABARD dairy credit potential. Afzalpur second due to high feed availability (tur husk) and low competition. Jevargi weakest due to flood/drought duality and distance.

seasonality.peak_period: October to February - post-monsoon green fodder abundance, higher milk yield
seasonality.low_period: March to June - summer fodder scarcity, heat stress reduces yield by 10-20%, water shortage
seasonality.reason: Kalaburagi semi-arid climate 770mm rainfall, 5-45C range per DDMP; green fodder scarce in summer, dry fodder price rises
seasonality.business_impact: Revenue may drop 15% in summer due to lower yield and higher feed cost
mitigation: Shade nets and foggers for shed

climate_factors: Heat stress above 35C reduces milk yield
Drought - erratic rainfall 770mm normal, actual 501-1068mm variation per PLP
Lumpy Skin Disease and FMD during humid season

climate_and_climate_change.business_impact: Reduced productivity, higher mortality risk, fodder shortage

assumptions.parameter: Milk yield per CB cow per day

assumptions.source/basis: KMF procurement Rs 33-35 plus Rs 5 incentive = Rs 38 effective; used 33 base + incentive separate
Karnataka govt incentive since 2016, KMEA evaluation

assumptions.parameter: Concentrate feed per cow per day
Vet and AI per cow per year

financial_model.calculation_methodology: Monthly Revenue = No of milch animals * avg yield * 30 days * (KMF rate + incentive) . For small 2 cows *10L*30=600L*Rs38=22800 expected. Expenses = feed (concentrate 4kg*26=104 + green 15kg*2=30 + dry 6kg*5=30 =>164 per cow per day) *30=4920 per cow, plus labour 3000, electricity 500, vet amortized 250, misc. Conservative assumes 8L yield, optimistic 12L and direct sale mix at Rs50.

strengths: High rural suitability - 70% population dependent on agriculture, dairy as supplementary per NABARD PLP
Assured market via 325 DCS and KMF union plus Rs 5/L state incentive since 2016
NABARD credit potential Rs 266.55 crore for dairy in district indicates bankability
Local feed availability - tur husk, jowar straw in Afzalpur/Aland
weaknesses: Water requirement 100-150 L/animal/day in semi-arid zone with 770mm rainfall
Low milk productivity - per PLP need crossbreeding improvement
Veterinary infrastructure gap - need more AI centres per PLP
Working capital intensive - feed cost 60% of expenses
opportunities: Karnataka Budget 2026-27 25% subsidy for 10,000 beneficiaries for cow/buffalo purchase in Kalaburagi division - Rs 40 crore earmarked
AHIDF 3% interest subvention for dairy processing/value addition up to 90% loan
Rashtriya Gokul Mission 50% capital subsidy up to Rs 2 crore for breed multiplication farm
Ksheera Sanjeevini women dairy scheme - KSRLPS + KMF targeting SC/ST/minority women
Nandini Ksheera Samridhi Bank planned in all taluks for low-interest dairy loans
threats: Climate - temperature 5-45C range, 41.8-44.5C heatwaves reported, reduces yield
Delayed incentive payments - 9 months delay reported in 2024
Increasing competition from private dairies and direct sales

seven_day_validation_experiment.objective: Validate dairy demand, input cost, and KMF linkage in chosen taluk before investing

days.target: Visit 5 villages, list 3 DCS and 2 private collectors, note procurement price and timing
days.measurement: Number of active DCS within 5km, price Rs/L

days.target: Talk to 20 households, 5 tea shops, 2 sweet shops in taluk HQ about milk need and price willingness
days.measurement: 10+ households willing to buy at Rs 48-50, 2 tea shops need 20L/day

days.target: Get quotes from 3 animal traders at Kalaburagi livestock market, 2 feed dealers for concentrate, green fodder
days.measurement: Animal cost Rs 55k-65k, feed Rs 24-28/kg, transport cost

days.target: Buy 5L milk from local farmer, test fat % via lactometer, try selling 5L in town
days.measurement: Fat 3.5-4%, sale time <2 hours, customer feedback

days.target: Offer 10 customers pre-order of 1L/day for next week, collect advance Rs 100
Use real quotes: Revenue = yield*price, Expense = feed+labour+transport, Profit per litre
days.measurement: Expected profit Rs 5-8/L after all costs, break-even <24 months

days.target: Decide Proceed/Modify/Do Not Proceed based on criteria
days.measurement: Proceed if 5+ pre-orders, supplier quotes within budget, DCS membership possible, profit >Rs 3000/month per 2 cows

success_criteria: At least 5 interested customers with advance
failure_criteria: No DCS within 5km and no direct sale demand
seven_day_validation_experiment.decision_rule: Proceed if success criteria met 3/4; Modify (change breed or scale or location to Kalaburagi/Afzalpur) if 2/4; Do Not Proceed if <2

national_level.implementing_ministry_or_department: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying
national_level.purpose: Incentivize investments in dairy processing, value addition, animal feed plants, breed multiplication farms
national_level.business_relevance: Dairy farm with processing/value addition or feed plant can get loan up to 90% project cost with 3% interest subvention for 8 years including 2 years moratorium; credit guarantee up to 25%
national_level.eligible_beneficiary: Individual entrepreneurs, private companies, MSME, FPO, Section 8 companies, Dairy Cooperatives
national_level.business_eligibility: Dairy processing and value addition, establishment of dairy units linked to processing is eligible
national_level.women_eligibility: Yes - women entrepreneurs eligible on same terms, no extra benefit but eligible
national_level.project_cost_limits: No minimum/maximum cap - loan up to 90% of project cost
national_level.loan_amount: Up to 90% of project cost from scheduled bank, NABARD, NCDC, NDDB
national_level.subsidy: Interest subvention 3% per annum for 8 years
national_level.interest_rate: Bank rate minus 3% subvention; effective ~7-8% if bank 11%
national_level.collateral_requirement: As per bank, credit guarantee up to 25% of borrowing from Rs 750 crore fund
national_level.current_status: Active - extended till 2025-26 with outlay Rs 29610.25 crore merging DIDF

national_level.scheme_name: Rashtriya Gokul Mission - Breed Multiplication Farm (Hub and Spoke)
national_level.implementing_ministry_or_department: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying

national_level.eligible_beneficiary: Individual, SHG, FCO, FPO, JLG, Section 8 companies
national_level.project_cost_limits: Subsidy up to Rs 2 crore per farm (50% of capital cost)
national_level.interest_rate: Eligible for AHIDF interest subvention additionally

capital_and_financing.recommended_funding_pathway: Small: Own 50k + KCC Animal Husbandry loan 1.5L from Karnataka Gramin Bank/SBI with NABARD refinance + apply for Karnataka 25% dairy subsidy via AH dept + KMF membership for Rs5/L incentive. Medium: AHIDF loan up to 90% with 3% subvention via scheduled bank + NLM 50% subsidy for fodder unit as backward linkage. Women: Ksheera Sanjeevini via SHG for 2-cow unit.
capital_and_financing.important_distinction: Business investment and government-scheme own contribution are different concepts.

final_feasibility.strongest_reason_to_consider: Kalaburagi taluk has highest demand due to urban market, best infrastructure (29 vet hospitals, 109 dispensaries, 572 DCS, APMC, 270 bank branches), NABARD dairy potential Rs 266 crore, and assured KMF procurement with Rs 5/L state incentive plus new 25% animal purchase subsidy in 2026-27 budget.
final_feasibility.biggest_risk: Summer fodder and water scarcity (semi-arid 770mm, 5-45C) plus feed cost 60-70% of expense and delayed incentive payments (Rs 606 crore pending reported) plus disease LSD risk
final_feasibility.minimum_viable_startup: 2 crossbred cows, investment Rs 1.75 lakh + working capital Rs 35k = Rs 2.1 lakh total, own contribution Rs 50k, loan Rs 1.5 lakh via KCC, break-even 22 months
final_feasibility.recommended_scale_for_beginner: Small scale - 2 cows with KMF DCS membership, own fodder cultivation, then scale to 5-10 cows after 1 year validation
final_feasibility.recommended_validation_before_investment: 7-day validation: map 5 villages DCS, interview 20 households, get 3 animal quotes from Kalaburagi market, secure 5 pre-orders, calculate unit economics
final_feasibility.loan_readiness: High - dairy is priority sector, NABARD refinance, KCC for animal husbandry, AHIDF 3% subvention, zero-interest up to Rs 2 lakh via cooperatives in Karnataka, DCS linkage improves bankability
